clue.text: Million on course? That's a lucky thing

parts.note: Ascot is an English racecourse, so 'on course' suggests the course itself

explanation.surface: A punter at the races asks whether a big win at the course is the lucky charm at work.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a famous racecourse in Berkshire, England; the question mark flags that 'course' is an example of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object believed to bring good fortune to a team or group.

clue.text: Ground about to be swamped by boundless watercourse

indicators.note: swamped means flooded over, so the short word is engulfed by the watercourse
without bounds means the ends of the word are removed

parts.note: a canal is an artificial watercourse
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A sports ground is about to be flooded by an overflowing stream.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed area for sport or entertainment, such as a stadium pitch.

clue.text: Jazz enthusiast has to suppress cause of pain in release of emotions

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz fan

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down or contain, so the has letters hold the cause of pain

parts.note: taken as written
RSI, repetitive strain injury, causes pain

explanation.surface: A jazz fan must hold back a painful condition while letting feelings out.
explanation.walkthrough: RSI is repetitive strain injury, an ache caused by repeated movements such as typing.
explanation.definitionFit: Catharsis is the purging of pent-up feeling, as through art or tears.

clue.text: Is subdued by remarkable English composer

indicators.note: in a down clue being held under means placed below, after the other piece

parts.note: tall, as in a tall story, means remarkable or hard to believe
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is overshadowed by a remarkable English composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Tallis was a Tudor composer of church music.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Tallis was a sixteenth-century musician from England, noted for choral works like Spem in alium.

clue.text: Advanced equipment in Welsh town will do for flowering plant

indicators.note: the advanced equipment sits inside the town's name, so 'in' places those letters within it

parts.note: Mold is a market town in Flintshire, north Wales
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
a rig is a set of equipment, as in a drilling rig

explanation.surface: A Welsh town is said to make do with modern kit when it comes to growing flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: MOLD is a small town in north Wales; 'will do for' simply links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The marigold is a common garden annual with bright orange or yellow blooms.

clue.text: Easy income this elderly guy perhaps makes at auction?

parts.words: this elderly guy perhaps makes at auction?
parts.note: a guy is also a rope steadying a tent, so an aged guy rope sold at auction earns cash for a worn cord

explanation.surface: An old man sells something at auction and pockets an easy profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elderly guy' looks like an old man, but a guy is a tent rope; selling old cord gives the phrase literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes earnings gained for very little effort or for something of no value.

clue.text: The various common soldiers, enthralled by a lot of sonorous oratory

indicators.note: enthralled means held captive, so the mixed letters and soldiers are held inside
a lot of means most, the final letter dropped

parts.note: a rich voice is deep and sonorous

indicators.note: various means the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: OR is other ranks, non-commissioned soldiers

explanation.surface: A deep-voiced speech captivates assorted ordinary troops.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, 'other ranks', is the British army term for soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is the art of persuasive speaking, eloquent speech of the kind called oratory.

clue.text: Individual interrupting old King will be somebody facing death

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so the individual sits within the king's letters

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: Someone who interrupts an old king is doomed.
explanation.walkthrough: GR is the royal cipher of King George, seen on old British postboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is a person or thing beyond saving, sure to die or be ruined.

clue.text: Dodgy tax rule I use initially offering delight

indicators.note: dodgy means suspect or crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A shady tax regulation, used from the start, brings pleasure to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offering' is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To luxuriate is to take great pleasure in something, to revel or delight in it.

clue.text: Epidemic? Change will involve steps

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or enclose, so the coins surround the steps

parts.note: pence are small coins, loose change
a stile is a set of steps for climbing over a fence

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an outbreak will force a change involving a series of measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like a verb in the surface but is the noun for loose coins; a stile is the set of steps over a field fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilence is an old word for a deadly infectious disease spreading widely, such as plague.

clue.text: Subsequent difficulty about kiss

indicators.note: the difficulty goes round the kiss, so 'about' means surrounding it

parts.note: a net is a snare or entanglement, a trap one struggles to escape
X is the kiss written at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A later problem arises around a kiss, a romantic complication.
explanation.definitionFit: Next describes what comes immediately after, following in order or time.

clue.text: Epic place where many live in wisdom

parts.note: a saga is a long epic story
a city is a large settlement with a big population

explanation.surface: An epic tale set in a crowded metropolis turns out to be full of wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagacity is keen judgement and discernment, a near synonym of wisdom.

clue.text: Scientific model compounded error with variable

indicators.note: to compound is to mix ingredients together, so the letters are blended into a new order

parts.note: Y is a conventional algebraic symbol for a variable

explanation.surface: A scientist's model has made a bad mistake even worse by adding an unknown quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compounded error' reads as making a mistake worse, but 'compounded' tells you to rearrange ERROR.
explanation.definitionFit: An orrery is a clockwork model of the solar system showing the planets moving round the sun.

clue.text: Spoils component of the foregoing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to mar is to spoil
second meaning: the planet ... is part of the model in the previous clue, an orrery

explanation.walkthrough: 'the foregoing' points back to the previous across answer, ORRERY, a model of the solar system that includes the planet Mars.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb mar means damage or impair, and the red planet features in any model of the solar system.

clue.text: A small group, American, holding company up? Dreadful

indicators.note: holding means the small group grips the reversed company within it

parts.note: a trio is a group of three

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: US means American

explanation.surface: A small American band props up a company, a terrible situation.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrocious means appallingly bad, horrifying or of very poor quality.

clue.text: First thing about the mouth when imbibing one drink

indicators.note: to imbibe is to take in drink, so the mouth word takes in the letters

parts.note: oral means concerning the mouth
I is the Roman numeral for one
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: The first thing about the mouth while someone is drinking is the drink going in.
explanation.definitionFit: Original can mean earliest or initial, existing from the beginning, as in the original owner.

clue.text: Popular newspaper possibly I start to consider as containing no life

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
an organ is a publication speaking for a group, a newspaper for example

indicators.note: the start of the word means its first letter

explanation.surface: A tabloid may make someone start to think it is lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Inorganic matter is not derived from living things, with no biological origin.

clue.text: Necessarily how military rations are allotted?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as two words, rations are issued ..., for each armed unit

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as PER FORCE to read it as a rule for sharing out army supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Perforce is an old adverb meaning by force of circumstance, inevitably.

clue.text: Get on with Antonio at the end? I do

definitions.text: Get on with Antonio at the end? I do

parts.note: to prosper is to get on, to do well

indicators.note: only the final letter of Antonio is taken, the end of that name

explanation.surface: A speaker claims to be reconciled with Antonio by the close of the story.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's The Tempest, Prospero is usurped by his brother Antonio and forgives him in the final act; the whole clue describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: The exiled duke of Milan in Shakespeare's play makes peace with his treacherous brother at the play's end.

clue.text: Fan's heading off for a measure of cricket?

indicators.note: the heading, the first letter, is taken off the fan word

parts.note: a lover is a fan or enthusiast, as in a music lover

explanation.surface: A cricket supporter leaves early and wonders whether a session has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan's' is Fan plus 's for 'is'; the fan is a LOVER, whose head comes off.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end, a unit of play.

clue.text: Toxic Cockney? It's as much as a member can take

definitions.text: as much as a member can take

indicators.note: a Cockney Londoner drops the h at the start of words

parts.note: harmful means toxic, poisonous

explanation.surface: A poisonous Londoner is asked whether this is the limit of what a club member can stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class East Londoners, famously drop initial H. The 'member' is an arm, a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: An armful is the quantity one arm, a limb, can hold, so member means limb here.

clue.text: Ragamuffin, in scrape, mustering resistance

indicators.note: to muster is to gather up, so the scrape gathers the resistance inside it

parts.note: a scuff is a scrape or graze
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A street urchin in trouble rallies to fight back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in scrape' looks like being in a fix, but the scrape is SCUFF, holding R.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruff is an untidy, dirty-looking person, much like a scruffy urchin.

clue.text: Female in military squad is not suitable

indicators.note: the female letter goes inside the squad word

parts.note: a unit is a military group

explanation.surface: A woman in an army squad is judged unsuitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfit means not suited or not good enough for a purpose or role.

clue.text: Take away agreed-to changes

indicators.note: changes means the letters of the fodder are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone retracts changes that had already been agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agreed-to' supplies its eight letters, AGREEDTO, which are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To derogate from something is to detract from it, lessening or taking away from its worth.

clue.text: Yonder article borders on remarkable

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outside letters, its first and last

explanation.surface: A piece of writing over there verges on the extraordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders on' looks like 'is close to' but takes the edges of 'remarkable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old-fashioned adverb meaning over there, at that distance.

clue.text: Demonstration quietly removed top of building

indicators.note: removed means the quiet letter is taken out of the demonstration word

parts.note: a proof is a demonstration that something is true
P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: Protesters were quietly taken off the top of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demonstration' suggests a protest, but it is PROOF in the sense of showing something true.
explanation.definitionFit: The roof is the covering structure forming the upper part of a house or other structure.

clue.text: Give up wrapping most of present for regular criminal

indicators.note: the giving-up word wraps around the shortened present like paper

parts.note: to render is to give up or surrender

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to offer is to present

explanation.surface: Someone stops wrapping most of a present for a hardened crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift noun in the surface but is the verb meaning to put forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A reoffender is a person who commits crimes again after conviction, a habitual lawbreaker.

clue.text: We run into a place? Kind of

indicators.note: into means the first pair of pieces goes inside the place

parts.note: a site is a place or location
taken as written
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A group dashes into a spot, sort of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We run into a place' reads as an action, but 'run' is the single-letter cricket abbreviation and 'into' is a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to soften a statement, meaning in a manner of speaking or so to say.

clue.text: Fruit, lightly cored, served with a lot of food

indicators.note: a cored fruit has its middle removed, so only the outside letters remain
a lot of means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: cheer is an old word for food and drink, as in good cheer

explanation.surface: A fruit is lightly cored and served alongside a big helping.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEER as food and drink survives in phrases like 'Christmas cheer'.
explanation.definitionFit: The lychee is a small Chinese tree fruit with rough red skin and sweet white flesh.
